fixes.explanation: Yes, it wilts. Verse 4 says, “Bashan and Carmel wither, and the flower of Lebanon wilts.” Bashan and Carmel are places, and they wither in the same verse. Just before that, “He rebukes the sea and dries it up; He makes all the rivers run dry.”
Not in this verse, friend. Nahum says, “Bashan and Carmel wither, and the flower of Lebanon wilts.” Nothing in that line stays fresh. The flower of Lebanon wilts, and that's the word to hold onto.
Right. Nahum says He will “…pursue His enemies into darkness.” Pursuing is the opposite of letting someone escape. It's a serious line, and Nahum doesn't soften it.

That's what he says. Verse 9 says, “Whatever you plot against the LORD, He will bring to an end.” Then it adds, “Affliction will not rise up a second time.” That's the promise: no second round of affliction.
Soaked is the opposite of dry, friend. The verse says, “…like stubble that is fully dry.” A soggy cookie is a sad cookie, and the stubble in this verse is the dry kind.

Green is a fine color for a lot of things, baker, but not this stubble. Nahum says, “…like stubble that is fully dry.” Picture a cookie left out so long it crunches when you look at it. That's the kind of dry he means: fully dry.

Locking up would be going the wrong way, friend. The LORD says, “For I will now break their yoke from your neck and tear away your shackles.” He's talking about taking Judah's shackles off. Tear away is the word in the verse.
Yes. The LORD's command says, “There will be no descendants to carry on your name.” That's what He says about Nineveh. It's a heavy word, and Nahum doesn't soften it.

Mountains show up in the verse, but not for hiding. Nahum says, “Look to the mountains—the feet of one who brings good news, who proclaims peace!” Then he says, “Celebrate your feasts, O Judah; fulfill your vows.” Judah is told to celebrate, not hide.
